newsitem.title: USA: Netcom sees average revs per customer up.
newsitem.headline: Netcom sees average revs per customer up.

text.p: Netcom On-Line Communication Services Inc on Monday said average revenue per subscriber rose 3 percent in the fourth quarter from the third and further gains were expected this year.
In reporting fourth-quarter results, Netcom said its average revenuue per subscriber was $21.04 per month.
Netcom President and Chief Executive David Garrison said average revenue per subscriber was expected to grow as more products and services became available to customers.

The figure is an important measure for Netcom, which is focusing less on increasing its total number of subscribers and more on increasing the average spent by each user on an growing array of services.

"In the fourth quarter, we further defined the way we intend to operate within this industry by focusing on providing quality services which enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of our customers," Garrison said in a statement.
"Under this model, subscriber growth has taken a back seat to other, more meaningful measures, such as average revenue per subscriber and revenue growth," he said.
Netcom made the remarks in reporting a fourth quarter net loss of $11.5 million, or a $0.99 a share loss, compared with a loss of $5.4 million, or $0.55 in the 1995 fourth quarter.

The fourth quarter result was more favorable than analysts had predicted. Wall Street's mean estimate was for Netcom to report a loss of $1.10 a share, according to First Call, with loss estimates ranging from $1.23 a share to $0.96 a share.
Local access numbers rose to 331, up from 210 at the end of 1995, and the average number of subscribers was 580,000, up from 308,000 at the end of 1995.
Netcom reported record revenue of $36.4 million for the fourth quarter, up 85 percent over the year-ago period and a 14 percent increase from the immediately prior third quarter.

Worldwide gross margins were 26 percent for the fourth quarter of 1996, compared with 24 percent in the third quuarter, incluuding both established U.S. businesses and startup operations in Britain and Canada.
Operating expenses as a percent of revenue decreased to 60.5 percent in the fourth quarter from 70.7 percent in the third, as a result of revenue growth and expense management, the company said.

Fourth quarter earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) improved by 50 percent over the third quarter to an EBITDA loss of $3.2 million. The company said its focus on cash management enabled it to diminish its cash burn to $12.7 million in the fourth quarter, a decline of 49 percent from the third quarter level of $24.8 million.
